articles.title: Quote of the day by Lionel Messi: "If I wasn't paid to be a professional footballer I would…" - famous words reveal why football was always more than just a career
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Lionel Messi's words capture the genuine, deep connection he has always had with football, and the kind of passion that has quietly defined his entire.
articles.body: Lionel Messi's words capture the genuine, deep connection he has always had with football, and the kind of passion that has quietly defined his entire extraordinary career. "Money is not a motivating factor," he said. "Money doesn't thrill me or make me play better because there are benefits to being wealthy. I'm just happy with a ball at my feet. My motivation comes from playing the game I love. If I wasn't paid to be a professional footballer I would willingly play for nothing." For Messi, the game has always represented something considerably more than simply a way of earning a living. Long before becoming one of the most recognised footballers in the world, he was simply a young boy who genuinely loved having a ball at his feet, and his eventual success, trophies and financial reward all came considerably later, arriving on top of a love for the game rather than as the actual reason for it.Quote of the day by Lionel Messi"If I wasn't paid to be a professional footballer I would willingly play for nothing"A real moment that tested this exact quoteIn 2021, this sentiment was tested in a genuinely real way. Messi's 21-year career at Barcelona, the only club he had ever known as a professional, came to an end because the club was unable to register his new contract under La Liga's financial rules during a serious financial crisis. He subsequently joined Paris Saint-Germain on a free transfer instead. Barcelona's president at the time, Joan Laporta, later told a radio station he had "hoped Messi would do a U-turn" and offer to play without a salary in order to stay at the club. Messi responded publicly that he was genuinely hurt by the comment, and insisted he had never actually been asked to play for Barcelona for free. It is a genuinely useful, real-world reminder that a sincere feeling about loving the game for its own sake, and the actual financial realities of professional football, can sit together in a considerably more complicated way than a single quote might suggest.Understand the meaning behind the quote by Lionel MessiMessi is saying that his own motivation to play football has never primarily come from money. Professional sport can genuinely provide enormous financial reward, but that reward was never really what makes someone actually fall in love with a game in the first place. His willingness to say he would play even without payment suggests the activity itself has always been its own genuine reward for him. Football was simply something he wanted to do, regardless of whether it ever came with a salary attached.Why passion can genuinely be more powerful than moneyMoney can provide real motivation, but it does not always create genuine enthusiasm on its own. Someone who genuinely enjoys what they do tends to be considerably more willing to spend real time practising, improving and working through a genuine setback, simply because the activity itself already has value to them regardless of outcome. Passion, in that sense, can become a genuinely powerful source of persistence. Messi's own career demonstrates how an interest that begins as something simply enjoyable can eventually become a profession at the highest level imaginable.Messi's love for football began long before any real fameMessi grew up playing football in Rosario, Argentina, joining Newell's Old Boys as a child before eventually moving to Spain to join Barcelona's youth academy and continue his development. At that stage, there were genuinely no guarantees he would ever become one of the world's greatest players. The game came first. His early years were centred on developing his actual ability and simply enjoying football, rather than on the fame and financial reward that only eventually followed much later.When your genuine passion becomes your actual professionNot everyone gets a real opportunity to turn a passion into an actual career. For those who do, though, there can be a genuine temptation to focus entirely on the professional side of the activity instead. Contracts, salaries, achievements and outside expectation can sometimes quietly overshadow the original reason a person actually started in the first place. Messi's quote is really a reminder to stay genuinely connected to whatever made the activity meaningful to begin with.Why enjoying the actual process genuinely mattersSuccess is often measured purely by the final result. In football, that might mean trophies, goals or individual awards. The real process behind those achievements, though, involves countless hours of genuine training and repetition that nobody outside ever really sees. If a person genuinely enjoys the activity itself, that process can become rewarding in its own right, which is exactly why passion tends to help people stay committed even when real progress feels genuinely slow.Why passion never actually eliminates hard workGenuinely enjoying something does not mean it will always feel easy. Professional football requires extraordinary levels of training, discipline and real sacrifice, and Messi's quote should never be read as suggesting that passion alone somehow produces success on its own. Instead, passion provides the actual reason to keep doing the hard work in the first place. When someone genuinely cares about an activity, the genuinely difficult parts tend to become easier to accept, simply because the underlying goal still feels meaningful throughout.What this quote teaches about finding genuine purposeThe idea reaches well beyond football entirely. A person might genuinely love writing, teaching, designing or helping other people, and that activity may begin as a simple hobby long before it ever becomes an actual profession. The genuinely important question is what still remains valuable even once no financial reward is attached to it at all. That question alone can reveal exactly where someone's genuine interest actually lies.How to apply Lionel Messi's lessonIdentify what you genuinely enjoy, thinking honestly about the activities you would still pursue even without recognition or money attached.Protect your own passion, and do not let external reward quietly become the only reason you continue doing something.Enjoy the actual process, focusing on genuine improvement rather than only chasing the final result.Practise consistently, since passion becomes considerably more meaningful once it is combined with real discipline.Stay genuinely connected to your original motivation, remembering honestly why you actually started in the first place.Do not measure everything purely in financial terms, since some activities genuinely have value that reaches well beyond income.Accept that difficult periods will happen, since loving something never actually means every part of it will feel enjoyable.Keep genuinely improving, since real interest tends to encourage lifelong learning almost naturally.Find genuine meaning in your work, since a career becomes considerably more fulfilling once it aligns with what actually matters to you.Let success be a genuine result rather than the only real purpose, since achievements are valuable without needing to be the entire reason for doing something.Why this Lionel Messi's quote matters todayPlenty of people spend years genuinely trying to find work that gives them both real financial security and genuine personal satisfaction at the same time. Messi's words offer a genuinely useful way of looking at that search. The ideal situation may well be finding something you would still genuinely want to do even if money were entirely removed from the equation. That does not mean financial stability is unimportant, as his own real experience at Barcelona later showed. It means that passion can give work a genuinely deeper sense of purpose than money alone could ever really provide. For Messi, football became his actual profession because he was exceptionally talented at it, going on to become the record holder for the most Ballon d'Or awards in the sport's history. The quote simply suggests that his real love for the game came considerably before the salary, the fame and the trophies ever did.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

At an August 31, 2026 hearing, his private attorneys were allowed to step away from representing him, and the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office was appointed in their place. Burke confirmed the change in court and pleaded not guilty again. The move comes after months of high-profile proceedings surrounding the death of 14-year-old Celeste Abigail Rivas Hernandez. The singer remains in custody without bail while the case moves forward. A judge had already found enough evidence for the charges to proceed after a roughly five-day preliminary hearing in July. His next hearing is scheduled for October 2026. The shift in representation also marks a major change from the earlier stage of the case, when Burke was represented by private attorneys including Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter.Why D4vd’s private lawyers are no longer handling the caseThe change in counsel happened during the August 31 arraignment or re-arraignment. The court determined that Burke qualified for appointed representation and brought in the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office. New counsel includes Walid (Fouad) Kandeel.Burke’s former lawyers said they still support him and indicated that there was no conflict behind the decision. They also said the choice to change representation was Burke’s own. That keeps the focus on the legal change itself rather than suggesting that the former team had suddenly turned against their client.The timing is also notable because the case has already gone through a major evidentiary stage. During the July preliminary hearing, prosecutors presented testimony and evidence covering digital records, forensic findings, purchases and other parts of their case. Judge Charlaine Olmedo found probable cause on all counts and ordered Burke to stand trial.What charges is D4vd facing?Burke has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder with special circumstances, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and unlawful mutilation of human remains. Prosecutors allege that he was involved in a sexual relationship with Celeste that began when she was 13, while he was 18.The homicide case centers on prosecutors’ claim that Celeste was killed in April 2025 after threatening to expose the relationship and damage Burke’s career. Her remains were later discovered in the front trunk, or “frunk,” of his Tesla in September 2025.Prosecutors have presented a case built around texts, photographs, location records, Uber data, purchase records, DNA findings and other forensic material. Burke’s defense has rejected the prosecution’s narrative and maintained his innocence.What happens next in the D4vd case?No trial date had been firmly set as of the August 31 hearing. The immediate next step is another court appearance in October, with reports placing that date around October 9 or October 19.The case now moves ahead with the public defender’s office leading Burke’s defense. articles.title: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook sends memo to employees; says: I am not leaving Apple, but I am...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Tim Cook signed off as Apple chief executive on Monday the way he ran the company for 15 years, calmly and with the credit pushed elsewhere. In a fare.
articles.body: Tim Cook signed off as Apple chief executive on Monday the way he ran the company for 15 years, calmly and with the credit pushed elsewhere. In a farewell memo to Apple employees on his final day in the job, Cook wrote that this was a moment he always knew would come, and that it was still hard to believe he was writing the words. John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO on September 1.The Tim Cook memo is notable for what it leaves out. There is no product tease, no roadmap, and no mention of AI, regulation or China, the three pressures that will shape Ternus's first year. Instead Cook spends most of it thanking staff, arguing that Apple's culture is the thing an annual report can never capture, and reaching back to Steve Jobs and his line about leaving a dent in the universe. The sentence employees were waiting for came late. He is not leaving Apple, he said, only stepping away from a role he has loved deeply.Tim Cook hands Apple to John Ternus, a hardware man and not a services oneCook saved his warmest paragraph for his successor. He called Ternus brilliant and capable, and said few people understand what it takes to build world-changing products the way Ternus does. Coming from a CEO long accused of running Apple like an operations manager, the choice of words is pointed.Ternus has been senior vice president of hardware engineering, overseeing the entire device line-up. Recent launches under him include the ultra-thin iPhone Air, the cheaper MacBook Neo, and AirPods with hearing health features. Apple also pulled its Mac mini and Mac Studio releases earlier in the year to meet AI-driven demand. The promotion reads as a bet on hardware execution rather than a pivot to services.Tim Cook is not leaving Apple, he is changing desksFrom Tuesday, Cook becomes executive chairman of Apple's board. He keeps the portfolio he was best at, managing governments in Washington and Beijing, at a point when tariff demands and political requests are landing on Apple's desk with some regularity.Cook took over from Jobs in August 2011. The 15 years since brought the Apple Watch, AirPods, and a vastly expanded iPhone, iPad and Mac business. On X, he told the Apple community that his title changes on Tuesday but his affection for them will not, and signed the memo: "With all I have and all I am, I am always. Yours, Tim."Here's Tim Cook's final memo to Apple employees, in fullTeam,Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words. I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn’t let this day pass without sending a note to you to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you’ve sent my way, for the way you’ve shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader.The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that.There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here. It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day.Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that’s the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our “dent in the universe,” as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world. How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am.As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership.I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make.I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world.With all I have and all I am, I am always.Yours,TimGet the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: A climber fell 15 to 20 feet on a 350-foot North Carolina cliff; a rescuer ran 1.5 miles through a gorge carrying blood to keep him alive

articles.body: A rescue volunteer made a remarkable 1.5-mile run while carrying critical whole blood to an injured climber during a major rescue operation in North Carolina.The volunteer covered around 1,000 feet of elevation in just 31 minutes as 24 agencies worked together to reach a climber who had suffered serious injuries after falling approximately 15 to 20 feet near Shortoff Mountain in Linville Gorge, Burke County.According to a social media post from Burke County Rescue Inc and Burke County Search and Rescue on August 30, the rescue operation began at around 9:30 a.m. after emergency crews were alerted to the injured climber.The patient was eventually airlifted to Charlotte for specialist trauma care and was reported to be in stable condition following surgery.Climbers were tackling a challenging routeThe climbing party had been ascending Dopey Duck, a 350-foot, three-pitch, 5.9 traditional climbing route on Shortoff Mountain.According to the rescue agency's account, the lead climber was attempting to place protection approximately 40 feet above a ledge when they suffered a lead fall of around 15 to 20 feet.The climber swung away from the rock face during the fall and struck an adjacent rock pillar.The difficult terrain and the nature of the injuries immediately presented rescuers with a challenging operation.A Burke Rescue paramedic/RN and EMT/Mountain Rescue Technician, together with a Burke EMS paramedic, responded to the area and established voice contact with the climbing party.Because of the patient's injuries and the difficult location, rescuers had to rappel down to reach the climber while additional emergency resources were requested.Volunteer races against time with whole bloodFollowing an assessment of the injured climber, rescuers determined that whole blood was needed to help stabilise the patient before transportation.That's when one Burke Rescue volunteer took on a critical task.The volunteer ran approximately 1.5 miles through difficult terrain while carrying the blood needed for the patient.In just 31 minutes, the volunteer covered around 1,000 feet of elevation before returning with the blood.The volunteer arrived before the patient was transported, allowing rescuers to use the blood to help stabilise the injured climber.The extraordinary effort became one of the defining moments of a rescue that involved 24 different agencies.Helicopter team airlifts injured climberFollowing the ground rescue operation, assistance was requested from the North Carolina Helicopter Aquatic Rescue Team (NCHART).NCHART aircraft “Kill Devil 244” successfully extracted the patient at approximately 2:45 p.m., according to the rescue agency.The injured climber was then transferred to an awaiting medical helicopter for continued treatment.Burke County Emergency Services later told News 13 on August 31 that the patient had been flown to an Atrium Health trauma centre in Charlotte.According to the patient's family, the climber was in stable condition following surgeries.Rescue crews faced long journey outThe operation did not end once the climber had been extracted.After the helicopter extraction, the remaining rescuers and members of the climbing party had to ascend the rope system back to the top of the route.They then began the long hike out of the area.The scale of the response highlighted the difficulties emergency crews can face when dealing with serious injuries in remote climbing locations.Burke County Search and Rescue later thanked all of the agencies involved in the operation.Officials issue safety reminder to climbersFollowing the rescue, Burke County Emergency Services also issued a reminder about the risks associated with climbing.“Please remember that climbing comes with inherent risks. Know your abilities, use appropriate safety equipment, and never underestimate the consequences of a fall,” the agency said in a social media post.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Posts invent false Palestinian, Israeli suspect in New Brunswick church fire
articles.summary: A clip of a historic church ablaze in Atlantic Canada spread on social media in posts claiming a migrant started the fire to target Canadian Christians. But...
articles.body:
A clip of a historic church ablaze in Atlantic Canada spread on social media in posts claiming a migrant started the fire to target Canadian Christians. But the allegations -- some of which said the suspect was Palestinian while others pinned blame on an Israeli -- are unfounded; the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) charged a 68-year-old local man with arson following the fire in New Brunswick.

"A 68 year old Palestinian Muslim migrant has just been arrested for burning down another church in Canada," claims an August 27, 2026 X post from Sean Feucht, an American Christian nationalist musician who had several Canadian concerts cancelled over safety concerns .

In the attached video, a church is seen in flames for several seconds before the spire collapses on the rest of the building.

Similar claims spread across Facebook , Instagram , Threads and X that a Palestinian migrant started a church fire in Saint-Simon, New Brunswick.

At the same time, other posts across networks claimed the arson was committed by an Israeli man in an "anti Catholic terror attack."

"A 68-year-old Israeli man has been charged with arson after the historic Saint-Simon Catholic Church in New Brunswick, Canada, was completely destroyed by fire," claims the caption of an August 28 Instagram reel .

AFP has repeatedly fact-checked similar claims about "Islamists" and migrants starting church fires in the United Kingdom and Canada .

Local media in Canada reported that the century-old church in Saint-Simon burned down on August 24 and the RCMP swiftly charged a suspect with arson for the conflagration.

But national police reports state that the accused is a local man, not a Palestinian or Israeli newcomer to Canada.

"Early in the investigation, police identified a person of interest, and a 68-year-old man from Saint-Simon was arrested," the August 25 RCMP press release says (archived here ). "The same day, 68-year-old Gilles Mallet appeared in Bathurst Provincial Court and was charged with arson."

He remains in custody , following an August 28 bail hearing.

Several Canadian churches have suffered serious damage from fires since 2021 (archived here and here ).

Multiple fires were reported following the 2021 revelation that ground-penetrating radar detected possible human remains at the former Kamloops Residential School in British Columbia, one of several Catholic boarding schools set up a century ago in Canada to forcibly assimilate Indigenous children (archived here and here ).

A CBC News investigation found 33 churches had burned down between May 2021 and December 2023, with only two ruled accidental. Fourteen of those fires took place on reserves and in First Nations.

Data from Statistics Canada shows a peak of 155 police-reported hate crimes targeting Catholics in 2021, but it does not indicate that Christians have been the main target of such offenses in recent yeas.

In 2025, the government agency reported that about 3 percent of religiously motivated, police-reported hate crimes in Canada targeted Catholics, while 71 percent were directed at Jewish communities and 18 percent at Muslims (archived here ).

articles.title: Israel Railways to cut Modi'in service this weekend to connect new 431 line to rail network
articles.summary: Upon its expected completion in 2028, Track 431 is anticipated to connect Jerusalem directly to the Shfela region and to Israel's southern coast, at a cost o...
articles.body:
Upon its expected completion in 2028, Track 431 is anticipated to connect Jerusalem directly to the Shfela region and to Israel's southern coast, at a cost of NIS 3.5 billion.

Modi'in's two train stations will face service disruptions this weekend as part of efforts to connect the new Track 431 project to the existing railway network, according to the Israel Railways website on Monday.

The service cuts affecting the Modi'in Center and Pa'ate Modi'in railway stations mirror disruptions in recent weeks as Israel Railways pushes ahead with the project, intended to connect Rishon Lezion to Modi'in and Jerusalem .

As part of the planned service disruptions, trains will not run between Modi'in and Ben-Gurion Airport from Thursday at 10:00 p.m. until Sunday at 4:00 a.m.

The railway noted that the line between Modi'in Center and Jerusalem Yitzhak Navon will run normally on Thursday night and Friday, while a free shuttle service will run between the Modi'in stations and Ben-Gurion Airport; the schedule is available here .

In addition, the Modi'in stations will be closed entirely on Saturday night, meaning the Modi'in-Jerusalem line will also not run, the railway said, though it was unclear if the closure is related to the Track 431 project.

Project completes rail ring around Gush Dan, includes longest bridge in Israel

The project runs largely inside the right-of-way of Highway 431, from which it gets its name. Upon its expected completion in 2028, Track 431 is anticipated to connect Jerusalem directly to the Shfela region and Israel's southern coast, as well as Rishon Lezion to Modi'in, at a cost of NIS 3.5 billion.

Once completed, it will join the existing Track 531, a loop line that connects Herzliya to Rosh Ha'ayin and Bnei Brak via Ra'anana and Petah Tikva, forming a complete railway ring around the congested Gush Dan region. The Eastern Rail Line, which was partially opened on June 28, connects the eastern end of the Track 531 loop to Israel's North and, eventually, South, bypassing the congested Tel Aviv Ayalon rail corridor.

Regarding the Ayalon corridor, a fourth track is being built to further increase railway capacity, with the projects complementing one another to strengthen Israel's rail system.

The 30 km line includes several station renovations and the addition of two new stations. One of these stations, Rishon LeZion - Tashach, will be located along a 3.5 km. bridge, the longest in Israel.

Existing Rishon Lezion stations under renovation, Ramle receives new station

The existing Rishon Lezion stations are being renovated to accommodate the new line, while a second Ramle station is being built south of the city to complement the existing station near the Ramle central bus station, which lies on the Beersheba-Lod-Tel Aviv line.

In February, the project reached a major milestone with the breakthrough of the Mevo Ayalon Tunnel, which connects the new Rishon LeZion - Tashach station to the coastal track, allowing trains to continue to Rishon Lezion - Moshe Dayan station and beyond.

The tunnel, which passes under Highway 20, stretches 400 meters and is one of two tunnels in the project; the other, the Ramla South Tunnel, has already been completed.

Track 431 is part of Israel Railways' "Connecting Israel" master plan for a rail service spanning from Kiryat Shmona in the North to Eilat in the South, with annual ridership expected to reach 300 million by 2050.

articles.title: 51 Indian nationals killed in Russian Army, 139 discharged; MEA says talks on with Moscow
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said on Monday that 139 of the 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces had been dischar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said on Monday that 139 of the 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces had been discharged, while 51 had died. India continues to have talks with Moscow to secure the release and repatriation of those still serving.Misri gave the figures while responding to a question on Indians serving in the Russian army during a Ministry of External Affairs briefing on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Kyrgyzstan.He said the issue of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian armed forces had been raised with Russia “at various levels on various occasions”.“At last count, we had information about 227 Indian nationals who had been recruited into the Russian army,” Misri said. “Out of that, we have information that 139 of our nationals have been discharged from the army. And unfortunately, of course, we have information also about 51 people who have perished so far.”Misri said India remained engaged with Moscow to secure the early discharge and return of those whose cases were still pending.“This is an issue that we are in constant discussions with the Russian side,” he said.He added that the Indian Embassy in Moscow was regularly monitoring the situation and working with Russian authorities to facilitate the release and repatriation of the remaining Indian nationals.“Our embassy in Moscow is monitoring this situation regularly with regard to the release and repatriation of these Indian citizens,” Misri said, adding that India was seeking to ensure that those still serving were discharged at the earliest and returned to their families.MEA's remarks come as PM Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation meeting in Bishkek.During the meeting, Modi stressed the need for the world to move from an era of “endless wars” towards the “end of war”, while the two leaders discussed bilateral cooperation and global developments.Misri also said India and Russia were looking to expand bilateral trade. He said an Indian Exporters Forum would be organised alongside the next annual summit in Russia to encourage Indian businesses to diversify and increase exports to the Russian market.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Kick streamer Treyliving recently confronted Twitch creator Nitro_Camden during an IRL livestream and bluntly called his content “boring.” The short exchange quickly spread online, with viewers divided over whether Trey’s criticism was fair. Nitro, who is only 18, defended himself by explaining that he has been making content for six or seven years and is trying to stay true to himself rather than change his personality for viewers. Trey later softened his stance, saying Nitro had continued to show him respect after their interaction and admitting that he may have been too harsh.Treyliving tells Nitro_Camden to be more entertainingThe interaction happened while Nitro_Camden was livestreaming. Treyliving approached him and gave his opinion on the young creator’s content without much buildup.“You still boring though bro,” Trey told Nitro.Nitro responded by explaining that streaming was not something he had just started doing because of his recent popularity. He said he had been creating content for years and was not interested in changing himself simply to create more dramatic moments.Nitro said:“Okay. Okay. All right, Trey. All right, Trey. Okay. You were saying I was trying to be somebody, but I’ve been doing this sh*t for like six or seven years. So you want me to pull up and knock somebody out? I am. I’m trying to be myself.”Trey still felt Nitro needed to work on his entertainment value.“You gotta be funny, bro. You gotta be funny, bro,” he said.The exchange led to different reactions online. Some viewers agreed with Trey and said Nitro’s streams were not entertaining enough, while others argued that the teenager was dealing with an unusually fast rise and needed time to adjust.One viewer wrote:“Sht he ain’t lying I went in that btch live and left immediately I’m not hating I just think his live is boring asf he don’t do much.”Another criticized Nitro for gaining an audience without gradually building one.Others defended him, with one viewer saying Nitro was “basically in panic mode” because he suddenly had to entertain a much larger audience than he had before.Nitro’s rise has been unusually quick. His breakout came after Stable Ronaldo raided his stream with around 15,000 viewers. He later passed 100,000 Twitch followers and has since grown to around 330,000 followers.Treyliving admits he may have been too harsh with Nitro_CamdenTrey later discussed the interaction during another livestream and gave more context for his comments.He said Nitro had actually shown him and his group plenty of support. According to Trey, Nitro even asked him for a picture after their interaction.Trey said:“He showed a whole lot of love to BAU, to me. He even asked for a picture. So, like, for me to, like, fold? He ain’t no folding. He ain’t no folding.”Trey also acknowledged that Nitro had been put in a difficult position by his sudden rise. Instead of slowly building an audience, Nitro found himself dealing with a large number of viewers in a short period.“This is how I feel. Like, bro really, like, just doing this sh*t. He got put in a position to where, like, he don’t know what to do. You hear me?” Trey said.He then admitted that Nitro’s continued respect made him rethink how he had handled the conversation.Trey added:“For me to come at bro like that, and he kept showing major love to me after what I said to him, it was just on some sht like, dmn. Like, that was some, you know, like, dmn. Like, you was on some p***.”The exchange has now become another discussion around Nitro’s rapid rise and the pressure that can come with suddenly having hundreds of thousands of followers.
